An examination is a careful, critical check of the system's actual condition and of whether it will stay safe until the next one.

The scheme must be drawn up, or certified as suitable for this system, by a competent person, must set the nature and frequency of examination, and must be reviewed at appropriate intervals.

summary: The owner of an Important Cultural Property must manage it as the Act, the Ministry of Education's ordinances and the instructions of the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs require (第31条第1項, art. 31(1)), and the Commissioner may give instructions on how it is managed (第30条, art. 30). summary: Altering the current state of an Important Cultural Property, National Treasures included, or doing anything that affects its preservation needs the prior permission of the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs; maintenance measures, emergency measures needed because of an extraordinary disaster and acts with only a minor effect on preservation are exempt (第43条第1項, art. 43(1)). The Commissioner may attach conditions to a permit and may stop the work or revoke the permit if they are broken (第43条第3項・第4項, art. 43(3)-(4)). Drilling bracket holes into the brick wall BW-251 of a National Treasure building alters its current state, so it must not start without permission.

summary: The owner or management body of an Important Cultural Property may prepare a conservation and utilisation plan that can include planned alterations, and ask the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs to approve it (第53条の2, art. 53-2). Work that the approved plan does not describe still needs a permit under 第43条 (art. 43).

summary: Unless a management body has been designated, the owner of a Historic Site manages and restores it (第119条第1項, art. 119(1)). The owner then has the same duties as for an Important Cultural Property, following the Act and the Commissioner's instructions and reporting damage within 10 days, and must also put up the signs, explanation boards, boundary markers, fences and similar facilities that Ministry standards require (第120条, applying 第30条, 第31条第1項, 第33条 and 第115条第1項). A designated management body carries equivalent duties (第118条, art. 118).

summary: The permission rule also covers Historic Sites: altering a site's current state, or doing anything that affects its preservation, needs the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs' permission, with the same exemptions for maintenance, disaster emergency measures and minor effects (第125条第1項, art. 125(1)). Anyone who goes ahead without permission, or breaks its conditions, can be ordered to restore the original state (第125条第7項, art. 125(7)). The whole Tomioka site is a designated Historic Site, so fixing sensor posts, cable runs or barrier anchors into its ground or structures falls under this article as well as 第43条.

summary: No California state agency may alter the original or significant historical features or fabric of a historical resource on the state master list, or transfer, relocate or demolish it, without first giving the State Historic Preservation Officer notice and a summary early in planning, after which the officer has 30 days to comment (§ 5024.5(a)). If the officer finds an adverse effect, the agency and the officer must adopt prudent and feasible measures to remove or reduce it (§ 5024.5(b)). Drilling brackets into the wall would need this consultation only if the building were state-owned and on the master list.

summary: Under California's environmental quality law, a project that may cause a substantial adverse change in the significance of a historical resource is treated as a project that may have a significant effect on the environment (§ 21084.1). Resources listed in or eligible for the California Register count, and those in a local register are presumed significant unless the evidence shows otherwise; which projects the division reaches was not checked, so this record only shows how California would weigh an alteration such as the BW-251 brackets.

summary: California provides alternative building regulations for repairing, altering, preserving or restoring qualified historical buildings, meaning buildings that a local or state government deems important to an area's history, architecture or culture, including those on national, state or local registers (§§ 18951, 18955). Repairs and alterations needed to preserve or keep using such a building may be made if they conform to this part, and local building departments and state agencies must apply its alternative standards when they permit the work (§§ 18954, 18959); state agencies also consult the State Historical Building Safety Board before decisions that affect a building's historical aspects (§ 18961).
